chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, who said: Abu Amr al-Zubayri narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'O Scholar, inform me: which deed is most virtuous before Allah?' He said, 'That which Allah does not accept any deed without.'
I said, 'And what is that?' He said, 'Faith in Allah, the One besides whom there is no deity. It is the highest in degree, the most noble in station, and the most abundant in reward.'
I said, 'Will you not inform me about faith? Is it speech and action, or speech without action?'

He said, 'Faith is entirely action, and speech is part of that action, by obligation from Allah. He clarified it in His Book, its light is clear, its proof is established. The Book testifies to it for one and calls one to it.'

I said, 'Describe it to me, may I be your ransom, so I may understand.' He said, 'Faith has states, degrees, layers, and stations. Among it is that which is perfect, its perfection being its end. Among it is that which is deficient, its deficiency being clear. Among it is that which is preponderant, its excess being greater.'

I said, 'Indeed, faith becomes perfect, deficient, and increases.' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'How is that?' He said, 'Because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made faith obligatory upon the limbs of the son of Adam, divided it among them, and distributed it within them. Thus, there is no limb of his but that it has been assigned a specific aspect of faith, different from what its sister limb was assigned.'

Among them is his heart, with which he understands, comprehends, and perceives. It is the commander of his body; the limbs do not return nor issue except by its opinion and command. Among them are his two eyes with which he sees, his two ears with which he hears, his two hands with which he grasps, his two legs with which he walks, his private part from which comes desire, his tongue with which he speaks, and his head upon which is his face. There is no limb among these but that it has been assigned a specific aspect of faith, different from what its sister limb was assigned, by obligation from Allah, Blessed is His Name. The Book speaks for it and testifies against it.

So He made obligatory upon the heart what He did not make obligatory upon the hearing. He made obligatory upon the hearing what He did not make obligatory upon the two eyes. He made obligatory upon the two eyes what He did not make obligatory upon the tongue. He made obligatory upon the tongue what He did not make obligatory upon the two hands. He made obligatory upon the two hands what He did not make obligatory upon the two legs. He made obligatory upon the two legs what He did not make obligatory upon the private part. He made obligatory upon the private part what He did not make obligatory upon the face.

As for what He made obligatory upon the heart of faith, it is affirmation, knowledge, conviction, contentment, and submission to the fact that there is no deity except Allah alone, without partner, a single God who has not taken a companion or a son. And that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and affirmation of what came from Allah from a prophet or a book. That is what Allah made obligatory upon the heart of affirmation and knowledge, and it is its action. And it is the Word of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Except for one who is forced while his heart is secure in faith, but whoever opens his breast to disbelief...'
Except for one who is forced while his heart is secure in faith, but whoever opens his breast to disbelief.
And He said: 'Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.'
And He said: 'Those who believe with their mouths but their hearts do not believe...'
And He said: 'Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills.'
That is what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, made obligatory upon the heart of affirmation and knowledge, and it is its action, and it is the head of faith.
And Allah made obligatory upon the tongue speech and expression of what the heart has concluded and affirmed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'And speak to people good words.'

And He said: 'And say, 'We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is One, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'' This is what Allah made obligatory upon the tongue, and it is its action.

And He made obligatory upon the hearing that it remain pure from listening to what Allah has forbidden, and that it turn away from what is not permissible for it from what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has forbidden, and from inclining to what angers Allah, Exalted and Mighty. So He said in that, having revealed to you in the Book: 'When you hear the verses of Allah being denied and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they enter into another topic...'
Then Allah, Exalted and Mighty, excepted the place of forgetfulness, saying: 'And if Satan should cause you to forget, do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.'
And He said: 'Give good tidings to My servants who listen to the word and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.'

And He, Exalted and Mighty, said: 'Certainly will the believers succeed. They who are during their prayer humbly submissive. And they who turn away from ill speech. And they who are about zakat are active.'
And He said: 'And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, 'For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds.''
And He said: 'And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by nobly.'
This is what Allah made obligatory upon the hearing of faith: that it does not incline to what is not permissible for it, and it is its action, and it is from faith.

And He made obligatory upon the sight that it does not look at what Allah has forbidden it, and that it turns away from what Allah has forbidden it from what is not permissible for it, and it is its action, and it is from faith.
So He, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their chastity.'
He forbade them from looking at their private parts, and that a man look at the private part of his brother, and he guard his private part from being looked at.
And He said: 'And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze and guard their chastity.'

That one of them does not look at the private part of her sister, and she guards her private part from being looked at. And he said: 'Everything in the Quran regarding guarding the private part is from fornication, except this verse, for it is from looking.'

Then he linked what He made obligatory upon the heart, tongue, hearing, and sight in another verse, saying: ' And you were not hiding that your hearing, your eyes, and your skins would testify against you.'

He means by skins the private parts and thighs. And He said: 'And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.'
This is what Allah made obligatory upon the two eyes of lowering the gaze from what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has forbidden, and it is their action, and it is from faith.

And Allah made obligatory upon the two hands that they do not grasp with them to what Allah has forbidden, and that they grasp with them to what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has commanded. And He made obligatory upon them charity, maintaining ties of kinship, striving in the cause of Allah, and purification for prayer.
So He said: 'O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles.'

And He said: 'When you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike their necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either [confer a favor] afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens.'
This is what Allah made obligatory upon the two hands, because striking is from their remedy.

And He made obligatory upon the two legs that they do not walk with them to anything of the disobediences of Allah, and He made obligatory upon them walking to what pleases Allah, Exalted and Mighty. So He said: 'And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful. And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.'

And He said regarding what the hands and feet testify against themselves and their masters for wasting what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, commanded and made obligatory upon them: 'Today We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn.'
This is also from what Allah made obligatory upon the two hands and upon the two legs, and it is their action, and it is from faith.

And He made obligatory upon the face prostration to Him by night and day in the times of prayer. So He said: 'O you who have believed, bow down and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good - that you may succeed.'
This is a comprehensive obligation upon the face, the two hands, and the two legs. And He said in another place: ' And the mosques are for Allah, so do not call upon anyone with Allah.'

And He spoke about what He made obligatory upon the limbs of purification and prayer with them. And that is because Allah, Exalted and Mighty, when He turned His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to the Ka'bah from the Sacred House, then Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed: 'Nor would Allah have caused your faith to be lost. Indeed, Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.'

So He named prayer 'faith.' Therefore, whoever meets Allah, Exalted and Mighty, preserving his limbs, fulfilling every limb of his limbs what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, made obligatory upon it, will meet Allah, Exalted and Mighty, with complete faith, and he is from the people of Paradise. And whoever is deficient in any of it or exceeds what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, commanded in it, will meet Allah, Exalted and Mighty, with deficient faith.

I said, 'I have understood the deficiency of faith and its perfection. From where does its increase come?' He said, 'The Word of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, 'Which of you has this increased faith?' As for those who have believed, it has increased them in faith, and they are rejoicing. And those in whose hearts is disease - it has increased them in filth, and they have died in disbelief.''
And He said: 'We relate to you, [O Muhammad], their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.'

And if it were all one thing, with no increase in it and no deficiency, then none of them would have preference over the other, and the favors would be equal in it, and the people would be equal, and distinction would be void. But by the perfection of faith, the believers enter Paradise. And by the increase in faith, the believers excel in degrees before Allah. And by deficiency, the negligent enter the Fire.'
I said, 'I have understood the deficiency of faith and its perfection.'
ai.seo_question: How does faith (Iman) manifest in the different parts of the body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Iman al-Jawarih' (Faith of the Limbs), establishing that belief is a comprehensive state encompassing cognitive conviction, verbal declaration, and physical action. By assigning specific Quranic obligations to each organ, the Imam demonstrates that faith is dynamic—capable of increase (ziyadah) and decrease (nuqsan)—thereby providing the theological basis for the gradation of believers' ranks in the afterlife.
